blueprint_topic: Management of Care — early individualized post-stroke rehabilitation planning versus very-early high-dose mobilization
stem: A nurse participates in rehabilitation planning during the early hospitalization of a client with acute ischemic stroke. Which approach best reflects current AHA/ASA guidance?

options.A: Begin interdisciplinary rehabilitation assessment during hospitalization and individualize mobility timing and intensity according to the client's condition and functional needs.
options.B: Use a standardized high-dose out-of-bed mobility schedule during the first 24 hours when the client is medically stable because earlier higher-dose activity improves recovery.
options.C: Wait until discharge planning is nearly complete before rehabilitation assessment so early spontaneous neurologic improvement does not affect the selected level of care.
options.D: Limit interdisciplinary rehabilitation assessment to clients with mild deficits and use medical stabilization alone to guide disposition for more disabling strokes.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline supports comprehensive multidisciplinary rehabilitation assessment during hospitalization to determine appropriate rehabilitation intensity and modality. The same guideline states that very early mobilization within 24 hours has not shown functional benefit and that high-dose very-early mobilization produced worse outcomes in the AVERT trial. Therefore, early rehabilitation assessment should not be converted into a universal high-dose mobility protocol; mobility timing and intensity should be individualized. B is incorrect because it applies the high-dose very-early mobilization strategy that lacked benefit and was associated with worse outcomes. C is incorrect because multidisciplinary rehabilitation-level assessment is supported during hospitalization rather than being deferred until discharge planning is nearly complete. D is incorrect because the need for coordinated rehabilitation assessment is driven by individualized impairment and functional needs and is not restricted to mild stroke.
educational_objective: Differentiate early inpatient rehabilitation assessment and individualized planning from indiscriminate high-dose mobilization within the first 24 hours after stroke; rehabilitation timing and intensity should reflect the client's condition and functional needs.
source_organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association
source_document_title: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
source_version_date: Originally published January 26, 2026; current free-access guideline rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: Section 5.7 Rehabilitation — Synopsis: patients have highly variable impairments and individualized needs; a comprehensive multidisciplinary program is critical for assessing appropriate rehabilitation intensity and modality; in-hospital interdisciplinary evaluation for the appropriate rehabilitation level is associated with improved functional outcomes; very early (<24 hours) mobilization has not shown functional benefit and high doses resulted in worse outcomes in one RCT. Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text 3: AVERT compared high-dose mobilization initiated within 24 hours with usual care and found fewer favorable 3-month outcomes in the high-dose very-early group; meta-analysis did not show functional benefit from very-early mobilization. Knowledge Gaps: optimal inpatient dose, frequency, and timing remain unclear.
source_claim_supported: Early multidisciplinary rehabilitation assessment is supported during hospitalization, but it should not be conflated with universal high-dose mobilization in the first 24 hours; mobility timing and dose require individualized clinical judgment.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care, printed page 7/PDF page 11: 'Identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members when providing client care'; 'Assess the need for referrals and obtain necessary orders'; 'Utilize resources to promote quality client care'; 'Coordinate client care across settings.'
pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan printed page 7/PDF page 11 visually verified by screenshot earlier in this 2026-08-20 audit session; no CACHE MISS. The AHA/ASA guideline was verified through the current free-access HTML version, so no guideline PDF was required as evidence.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'very early mobilization 24 hours stroke rehabilitation individualized planning AVERT' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the item to distinguish assessment/planning from mobilization dose without using universal or absolute-word distractors. The key no longer carries an extreme length cue, and distractors now test plausible errors in very-early high-dose mobility, delayed rehabilitation assessment, and severity-gated team assessment.

option_audit.A: Correct; integrates supported inpatient multidisciplinary assessment with individualized mobility timing/intensity and avoids an unsupported fixed-dose protocol.
option_audit.B: Plausible 'earlier is better' misconception; incorrect because high-dose very-early mobilization did not improve outcomes and was harmful in AVERT.
option_audit.C: Plausible wait-for-recovery misconception; incorrect because inpatient rehabilitation assessment is supported before discharge planning is nearly complete.
option_audit.D: Plausible severity-triage misconception; incorrect because coordinated rehabilitation assessment is not limited to mild stroke.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All options contain comparable timing and planning detail; the correct answer is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four options are parallel rehabilitation-planning actions.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after AHA/ASA source-based reread.
